issues.legal_issue: A claim to divide jointly held movable property into shares, where no particular item is immediately claimable in specie, is governed by the residuary limitation period rather than the period for recovery of specific movable property.
material_facts: The claimant and the other holder were entitled to movable property jointly and later as tenants-in-common.
A decree declared the claimant’s right to a share of the property but did not identify particular items to be allotted to either holder.
The claimant sought division of the property and transfer of items making up his share; he could not demand possession of any particular item before division.
issues.conclusion: The suit was in substance for division of jointly held movable property, not recovery of specific movable property wrongfully taken or withheld. It was governed by Article 120, not Article 49, of the Indian Limitation Act, 1908.
issues.legal_principle: Article 49 applies only where a claimant is entitled to immediate possession in specie of specific movable property that the defendant has wrongfully taken or is wrongfully withholding. A suit by one heir against others to separate and recover a share of movable estate is governed by Article 120 when no other specific article applies. The Court relied on Mohomed Riasat Ali v. Musummat Hasin Banu (1893) and distinguished Gopal Chandra Bose v. Surendra Nath Dutt (1908), where the defendant had no right or interest in the property and no right to retain it.

predicates.movable_share_division_suit: The claimant brought a suit seeking division and allotment of a share of movable property held jointly or in common.
predicates.property_not_divided_into_specific_items: The property had not been divided so as to identify particular items belonging to each holder.
predicates.claimant_not_entitled_to_immediate_posse: Before division, the claimant could not demand immediate possession of any particular item as his separate property.

issues.definition: When a suit seeks division of movable property that has not been divided into specific items and the claimant cannot immediately claim a particular item in specie, the residuary limitation period governs the suit.

issues.legal_issue: Time spent diligently and in good faith pursuing a civil proceeding founded on the same cause of action must be excluded when the proceeding cannot be entertained because of a jurisdictional defect.
material_facts: The claimant first sought to enforce his declared share through execution of a decree.
He pursued the execution proceeding in the subordinate court and on appeal, seeking the same substantive relief as in the later suit.
The execution proceeding ultimately failed because the decree had been made by a court lacking jurisdiction, and the defect prevented the executing court from entertaining the proceeding.
The claimant prosecuted the execution proceeding diligently and in good faith, and the later suit was founded on the same right.
issues.conclusion: The claimant was entitled to exclude the time spent in the execution proceeding, from its inception through its final disposal by the High Court, under section 14(1) of the Indian Limitation Act, 1908; with that time excluded, the suit was within the limitation period.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(1) of the Indian Limitation Act, 1908, excludes time spent prosecuting with due diligence and in good faith another civil proceeding against the defendant, founded on the same cause of action, in a court unable to entertain it because of a defect of jurisdiction or a cause of like nature. The exclusion covers proceedings in courts of first instance and appeal.

predicates.suit_follows_failed_civil_proceeding: The claimant brought a suit after an earlier civil proceeding against the same defendant failed.
predicates.prior_proceeding_founded_on_same_cause: The earlier proceeding and the suit sought to enforce the same underlying right against the defendant.
predicates.prior_proceeding_prosecuted_diligently_a: The claimant pursued the earlier proceeding with due diligence and in good faith.
predicates.prior_court_unable_to_entertain_for_juri: The earlier proceeding could not be entertained because the relevant court lacked jurisdiction.

issues.definition: When a suit follows a diligently and honestly pursued civil proceeding based on the same cause of action that could not be entertained for a jurisdictional defect, the time spent on that proceeding is excluded from computation of limitation.
